content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"Several links from evidence to conclusion are documented (the 7 of 19 essential functions, the FOHS reversal, RMO6's statement that the position description did not change), but the record itself notes the agency never delineated an undue hardship analysis, the 'individual assessment' is only possibly the FOHS evaluation, and the FY2015 evaluation is missing, so the path to the denial and to the 'Unacceptable' rating cannot be fully reconstructed."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Many characterizations are attributed to named officials (RMO1's productivity concerns, S1's evaluation quotes, FOHS doctor's statements), but others rest on hearsay (RMO2 testified to what she heard), unsourced claims (RMO1's 'low productivity' lacks cited metrics), and ambiguous references (S1's 'headquarters', unclear telework status)."},"rc3":{"status":"pass","note":"The record gives a dated sequence from the 2009 diagnosis and 2016 relocation order (Sept 27, 2016) through the Jan–Aug 2017 accommodation requests, denials, and appeals, plus the FY2013–FY2017 evaluation dates and the Feb 23, 2018 FAD request, with only minor gaps such as the approximate 2010-11 telework date."},"rc4":{"status":"gap","note":"Decision-makers are inconsistently identified (RMO3 claims the reassignment decision, RMO6 retired and was not contacted by the investigator and later testified differently, RMO4 chose not to articulate undue hardship factors), management gave no response to Complainant's Miami alternatives, the criteria for the PIP and ratings are not shown, and the FAD itself states a conclusion without any reasoning."},"rc5":{"status":"gap","note":"Because the FAD gives only a bare conclusion of no discrimination, the missing FY2015 evaluation, the undelineated undue hardship basis, unaddressed alternatives, and unresolved factual ambiguities mean an independent reviewer could not assess whether the record supports the conclusion without outside context."}}}
